subject: Clarify: training use of customer content and retention expectations
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@finserve.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataPrivacy <dataprivacy@finserve.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 15:01:00 +0000
Subject: Written confirmation re: training on customer content + retention questions

Hi Priyom,

We're preparing our vendor security review and need a clear written statement for our legal and privacy teams. Can you confirm the following for Redwood Inference's hosted service?

1) Does Redwood ever use customer-provided content (prompts, files, transcripts, or generated outputs) to train or update Redwood models by default? If yes, under what circumstances?

2) What are the default retention windows for: request/response logs, embeddings, KV caches, and longer-term backups? Are any of these retained beyond the customer session lifecycle?

3) If we request deletion of all data for an account, what is the end-to-end process and timeline? Do backups or cold storage copies extend this timeline?

4) Do these answers change if we move to Dedicated or Private deployment?

Please reply with succinct, actionable points and any relevant artifacts (DPA, SOC2 summary, data flow diagram). Thanks — we're trying to close this item by the end of next week.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of Vendor Risk — FinServe
elena.martinez@finserve.com


From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@finserve.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Written confirmation re: training on customer content + retention questions

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below are direct answers with the operational caveats. I can provide a short attestation PDF if that helps.

1) Do we use customer content to train/update models?
Short answer: No, we do not use customer-provided content from hosted accounts to train or fine-tune Redwood models as a default. Customer content stays in the customer workload and is not added to model training corpora unless there is an explicit, documented opt-in. Examples of opt-in: they sign a separate agreement to share anonymized transcripts for general model improvements, or a customer arranges a research collaboration.

2) Default retention windows (hosted):
- Request/response logs: 30 days by default (used for billing, debugging, and SLOs).
- Embeddings: Not persisted by default unless the customer uses the embeddings storage option; if persisted by customer choice, retention follows their storage config — otherwise the ephemeral embeddings used in-session are discarded immediately after the session ends.
- KV caches: Ephemeral by default — stored in-memory per session and cleared once the session terminates.
- Backups/snapshots: Operational backups (storage-layer snapshots) may exist for disaster recovery; lifecycle policy is 90 days by default. These are encrypted and access-controlled; we have processes to ensure deletion requests cascade to snapshot lifecycle where practicable.

3) Deletion process & timeline:
- Customer triggers account deletion or submits a 'delete all data' request via console or support.
- We remove active copies within 24–72 hours (most customer-visible resources).
- Snapshots/backups: asynchronous lifecycle — typically up to 90 days for full removal from backups depending on storage provider constraints. We can provide a deletion certificate that documents the steps taken (and an estimated final purge date) and prioritize expedited deletion under contract.

4) Dedicated & Private:
- Dedicated: Same default policy (we will not train on hosted data). Data isolation improves, and you can request tighter backup retention via enterprise config.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood's control plane can be configured to operate without any data exfiltration to Redwood-managed storage. In on-prem installations, training/telemetry collection does not occur unless explicitly enabled by the customer.

Operational notes & exceptions:
- Aggregated, telemetry-only signals (e.g., anonymized performance metrics, failure rates) may be used to improve the service; these do not include raw customer content and are not used to train language models.
- If a customer opts into a model-improvement program, we require a separate opt-in agreement and will provide a data handling addendum.

I'll attach our DPA, a SOC2 summary, and a simplified dataflow diagram. Happy to convert this into a short attestation letter for your records.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (DPA), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (summary), dataflow_finserve.png (diagram)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Written confirmation re: training on customer content + retention questions

Quick technical clarifications for the response: 
- Embeddings: By default, the embeddings endpoint returns vectors and we do not persist them server-side unless the customer uses our embeddings-storage feature or we have an explicit integration (e.g., vector DB addon). In-session vectors are memory-resident and cleared after the request lifecycle.
- KV cache: purely in-memory per inference instance; we intentionally avoid persisting cache to disk except in Dedicated environments where customers may enable persistence for performance; if persistence is enabled, retention follows the customer's config and we surface it during onboarding.
- Backups/snapshots: our S3 lifecycle is 90 days; some legacy environments have longer retention due to partner constraints — we should flag legacy accounts.
- Deletion: final purge from immutable snapshots can be constrained by the object storage provider; we mark objects for deletion immediately and document the lifecycle timestamp. For expedited requests we can coordinate with infra to exempt the account from future snapshots and accelerate lifecycle rules.

I'll draft one short paragraph you can paste into a customer attestation. Also recommend offering a deletion certificate with timeline windows and an option in contracts for an accelerated purge addendum.

-Rishi

Lauren's note (inline): Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> From a commercial/legal perspective, offering a deletion certificate + explicit opt-in for model improvements is ideal. We should include template language and an addendum that allows customers to buy accelerated backup purge as an enterprise control.

Subject: Re: Written confirmation re: training on customer content + retention questions — follow-up and artifacts

Elena — following up with the concise, customer-facing summary and the artifacts attached. Please find the key points below that you can use in your vendor intake form: 

- Training: Redwood does not use hosted customer content (prompts, uploads, transcripts, or output) to train or fine-tune models by default. Any use for model improvement requires an explicit opt-in and a separate agreement.
- Retention (hosted defaults): request/response logs 30 days; KV cache ephemeral (session-only); embeddings not persisted unless customer enables persistent embeddings storage; backups/snapshots lifecycle ~90 days.
- Deletion process: active copies removed within 24–72 hours; snapshot/backups purged per lifecycle (up to 90 days); deletion certificates and expedited purge addenda are available under enterprise contracts.
- Dedicated/Private: same non-training guarantee for hosted data; Private/on-prem installs can be configured so that no customer data leaves customer-controlled infrastructure.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (DPA), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf, dataflow_finserve.png. If you'd like a formal attestation letter signed by our security team, let me know and we'll produce one. We can also schedule a 30-minute call with Rishi to walk through the technical controls.

Thanks — happy to iterate if your legal team needs different wording.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
